title: Meals You Can't Miss
editorial: Malaysia may have been the easiest country on this trip to build an itinerary around eating.
Start with nasi lemak. It is oily, yes, but also a surprisingly complete meal with rice, sambal, egg, fish or meat and accompaniments.

Then satay. We had excellent beef skewers on Jalan Alor for RM20 per ten sticks. From there, lose discipline: mee goreng, seafood, cockles, frog, oysters and whatever the stall in front of you is grilling.
We ate at Heritage Kopitiam, Mansion Tea Stall, Good Timing, Restoran Meng Kee Grilled Fish and Warung Mry among others.
